title: In the Drops: New Shimano shoes and pedals, CeramicSpeed pulley wheels, Newmen’s wide wheels and an in-between Assos jacket

In the Drops: New Shimano shoes and pedals, CeramicSpeed pulley wheels, Newmen’s wide wheels and an in-between Assos jacket

As Microsoft has decided not to start its weekend early like it did last Friday, it’s back to business as usual for In the Drops in its Friday slot. As staff writer Ewan’s edition was the casualty of last week’s outage it was delayed to this Monday, so you get product round-ups to bookend your working week this week, you lucky lot.

I helped Ewan start the week off right with a complete history of Cannondale’s CAAD platform, then on Tuesday Ewan was back at the pumps reporting on Rapha’s return to the pro peloton with Red Bull-Bora-Handsgrohe.

We looked into where on earth once-touted wonder material graphene has gone in the bike industry on Wednesday, as well as published the first of eight mudguard reviews that have carried us through until today, with a brief pitstop to look into the rise of 32in gravel bikes.

Without further ado, let’s crack on with the second In the Drops of week 47.

Shimano S-Phyre RC910 shoes and Dura-Ace SPD-SLR pedals

The minty freshness of Shimano’s fifth generation S-Phyre shoes might catch the eye, and not without reason: Shimano claims they’re a few grams lighter and there’s a revised Boa cable path and carbon fibre heel cup to improve foot security. They also now use Shimano’s ‘Dynalast 2.0’ shape, which is wider at the toe and forefoot by 3mm and 2mm respectively, which the brand says helps the rider’s toes to splay more naturally, increasing comfort.

The real news here though is Shimano’s new pedal system, which sees its first major change in 23 years. SPD-SL moves to SPD-SLR, introducing several updates.

‘The pedal itself is stiffer and rotates more freely, but surfaces on both the cleat and pedal have also been altered to create a 2.3mm lower stack height. The rider’s foot is closer to the pedal axle, creating a more stable pedalling platform and improving power transfer,’ says Takao Harada, road and gravel product manager at Shimano Japan.

The pedal tip has a wider catch zone and the body is said to hang a slightly steeper angle (closer to vertical), both features that Harada says makes clipping in quicker and more natural. The cleat has been slimmed down and the necessary mounting hardware has been halved – this now no need for the washers between cleat and cleat bolt – reducing weight by 32g for a pair (142g versus 110g). This does mean fore-aft positioning is now limited to that which is baked into your shoe sole though (the new S-Phyres have increased adjustability in this area).

As Mathieu van der Poel will tell you as a result of his issues at Paris-Roubaix this year, the new system is not compatible with SPD-SL, though that will still be offered at 105 level, with Dura-Ace and Ultegra pedals moving to SPD-SLR.

CeramicSpeed Alpha pulley wheels

CeramicSpeed’s new Alpha PW upgrade kit looks to be a simple entry point to the Danish brand’s range of products, in that they can be a straight swap for a derailleur’s existing pulley wheels (CeramicSpeed’s complete OSPW cages generally require a new chain).

They are also half the price of OSPW systems, despite incorporating many of the same features: the ‘ADR’ debris-removing shape, a durable composite body that is claimed to last five times longer than stock and of course, the brand’s signature hybrid ceramic bearings.

The Alpha pulley wheels are said to lower bearing drag by 20% versus stock and come with a lifetime warranty. Along with the newly-released Alpha wheel bearings, this means that all of CeramicSpeed’s products are now backed as such.

Newmen Streem G.62 wheels

With its G.62 gravel race wheelset, German brand Newmen is doubling down on the theory that wider is better. The external width of the rims is a chunky 45mm, which Newmen claims produces aerodynamic results superior to rival wheels from Zipp and DT Swiss, so long as the right tyre is used.

‘You could use a tyre wider than 45mm, however the front wheel setup is fastest when the tyre is slightly narrower than the rim,’ says Bob Hoogerbrugge, Newmen’s brand manager. ‘Though the external dimension is wide, internally the wheels are more conventional at 27mm. The delta lets us make the bead hook portion of the rim walls very wide. They’re hollow though, so weight isn’t impacted, but the extra surface area goes a long way to prevent pinch punctures and improves rim durability against strikes.’

Newmen has also gone to the trouble of concealing the valves within the rim to eke out more speed – 0.5 watts according to Hoogerbrugge – and the rims are hooked, which sets them apart from many gravel wheelsets.

‘They are the safer solution as they do not require any special considerations of tyre compatibility,’ says Hoogerbrugge. ‘Hookless rims are primarily being offered because they are significantly easier to manufacture.’

Even with a hooked rim and a 62mm rim depth, the claimed weight is still competitive at 1,530g for the wheelset, thanks in part to carbon spokes, which Newmen says can produce the same level of stiffness as steel while using fewer spokes.

Assos Equipe Thermobooster P1 jacket

With a record-breaking summer almost still tingling the skin, Assos has reworked its jersey/jacket hybrid to reduce its weight.

‘We noticed riders on start lines wearing a spring jacket over their race suit to stay warm,’ says Luca Zanasca, senior manager of R&D Assos. ‘We wanted the Thermobooster to combine insulation with breathability without the bulk of a traditional recycled textile.’

Catering to the balmy autumn season – Assos says it works best between 12-21°C for rides that start cold and end warm – the updated Equipe Thermobooster P1 jacket combines the Sens Air Plus textile for the torso with a different sleeve material.

‘This Sens fabric is lightweight, non-brushed and highly elastic while also providing UPF 50+ protection,’ says Zanasca. ‘We think it’s not quite right that aero performance tends to be confined to summer outfits, so we’ve used our racing aero fit here too. On cooler days there’s still a need to be as fast as possible. The 575CX fabric on the sleeves has a 3D stripe structure and a second-skin fit, which makes it significantly more aero than a standard autumn jacket, plus we found that long sleeves are particularly fast between 35-45kmh.’
